rationale: The uniform-case bound recorded earlier rests on the ordering between the leader's lease expiring and a peer's election timer expiring, so its sharpest test is the tightest configuration ValidateConfig allows: an election timeout one millisecond above the lease. That configuration is uniform, legal, and removes almost all the slack the separation has been relying on, so it is the boundary that decides whether the mixed-timer finding is about timers differing at all or specifically about a voter's timer being shorter than the leader's lease. The probe is submitted for a retained execution with its question registered; the local dry run is native feedback only and is described as such.

investigations.question: With every node on identical settings but an election timeout only one millisecond above the leader's lease, does the separation between the cut-off leader's confirmation window and a competing election survive, or does the near-tie let a peer's timer win before the lease check fires?
investigations.hypothesis: The separation should survive even at a one-millisecond margin, because the two events are not independent: a peer cannot campaign until its own heartbeat timer expires, which is the election timeout it was configured with, and the leader's lease expires after its own lease timeout measured from the same last contact. With the lease shorter than the election timeout the lease still expires first, though the leader's lease check runs on a timer chain whose cadence can add up to the minimum check interval, so the margin is not unbounded and a violation would be informative rather than surprising.
investigations.discriminator: Run the plain uniform trial - no pre-existing campaign, settings heartbeat 50ms, election 51ms, lease 50ms - sixteen times and record whether any confirmation follows the appearance of a competing leader. A clean result keeps the boundary on the inequality between a voter's election timeout and the leader's lease; a violation with a witness would widen the defect to uniform clusters whose timers are merely close.

scope.description: Sixteen trials on hand-built four-node clusters whose nodes all share heartbeat 50ms, election 51ms and lease 50ms - the tightest uniform configuration ValidateConfig accepts. Each trial forces leadership onto node 0, demotes node 3 to nonvoter, records a baseline confirmation, applies one command, isolates the leader and the nonvoter from the two remaining voters in both directions, and polls the verification path every 2ms while watching those voters for a leader.
assumptions: The configuration is uniform and legal: the lease is at most the heartbeat timeout and the election timeout is at least the heartbeat timeout, so ValidateConfig accepts it on every node.
The trials start from a stable cluster with freshly reset follower timers, so the measured relation is between the lease expiry and the earliest legal campaign, not between arbitrary phases.
Verification is driven through the same channel the exported API uses; a competing leader is detected by reading the two isolated nodes' states.
The dry run is native feedback only; the retained execution is what a later interpretation would rest on.
excluded: No on-disk store, no network transport and no multi-process execution.
Only this one timer relation is exercised; the mixed-timer case is covered elsewhere in the run.

parameters.recorded_operands: adverse, preexisting_candidate, campaigner_state, campaigner_term, leader_term, polls, confirmations, last_confirmation_ms, first_peer_leader_ms, confirmations_after_peer_leader, confirmation_after_peer_leader, leader_stepped_down

experiment.prefix: Each trial builds four nodes by hand with identical settings of heartbeat 50ms, election 51ms and lease 50ms, waits for any leader, transfers leadership to node 0 and waits until it reports Leader, demotes node 3 to nonvoter with DemoteVoter and waits, records a baseline confirmation through the verification channel the exported API uses, and applies one command. It then disconnects the leader and the nonvoter from the two remaining voters in both directions, polls the verification path every 2ms while the leader still reports Leader, records the last confirmation's elapsed time and the first time either remaining voter reports Leader, and emits one summary event per trial with the counts, the terms and whether any confirmation followed a competing leader.

comparisons.description: Control at the tightest legal margin: no confirmation follows a competing leader. A violation with a witness would be the case that widens the defect to uniform clusters.
